questions.skill: Precise definition of parallel lines
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Write a precise definition of parallel lines.
questions.prompt_markup: Write a precise definition of parallel lines.
questions.correct_answer: Two lines are parallel if they lie in the same plane and do not intersect.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent wording. Essential: in the same plane, and no point in common. Not accepted: "lines that never meet" without the plane (skew lines in space never meet), or "lines that point the same way" (not precise).

questions.prompt: Box ABCD-EFGH has top face ABCD directly above bottom face EFGH (A above E, B above F, C above G, D above H). Using the definition, decide whether line AB is parallel to line HG, and whether line AB is parallel to line FG. Explain each.
questions.prompt_markup: Box ABCD-EFGH has top face ABCD directly above bottom face EFGH (A above E, B above F, C above G, D above H). Using the definition, decide whether line AB is parallel to line HG, and whether line AB is parallel to line FG. Explain each.
questions.correct_answer: AB ∥ HG: they lie in one plane (the slanted plane through A, B, G, H) and do not meet. AB and FG are not parallel: they never meet but do not lie in one plane (they are skew).

sections.skill: Prove that lines are parallel from angle facts

branch.new_demand: Use angle facts with a transversal to prove that two lines are parallel, instead of only applying the definition.

questions.skill: Prove that lines are parallel from angle facts
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Lines ℓ and m are cut by transversal t, and a pair of alternate interior angles are congruent. Explain why ℓ and m cannot meet (so they are parallel).
questions.prompt_markup: Lines ℓ and m are cut by transversal t, and a pair of alternate interior angles are congruent. Explain why ℓ and m cannot meet (so they are parallel).
questions.correct_answer: ℓ ∥ m
questions.required_method: Argue by contradiction: if they met, they would form a triangle with an exterior angle equal to a remote interior angle.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: assume ℓ and m meet at P; then t, ℓ, m form a triangle in which one of the congruent angles is an exterior angle and the other a remote interior angle; the exterior angle theorem (or the angle sum) says the exterior angle is larger, a contradiction. Alternative: cite the alternate interior angles converse with the parallel postulate.
questions.set_target: Write, repair, and apply a precise definition of parallel lines (coplanar lines that do not intersect)
questions.target_skill: Prove that lines are parallel from angle facts
questions.alignment_type: cross-standard extension; direct
